messages:
Ava Morgan: Quick continuation from yesterday's architecture triage. We need a concrete NUMA-aware prefetch + demote plan before we touch the allocator API. Idea: tag allocations with preferred_numa and a soft_tier (VRAM|HOST|SHARED). Evictor prefers non-preferred nodes first, and prefetch actively to preferred_numa when access rate > threshold.

Liam O'Connor: Sounds promising. Two questions: how do we measure/access rate cheaply? And how does this interact with our current continuous-batching (we don't want prefetch to amplify bursts).

Hiro Tanaka: For access rate we can sample LRU hits per-key over sliding window (exponentially decayed). Cheap counters per-bucket. Prefetch policy: only prefetch if sampled_rate>R and model latency budget allows (i.e., tail slack). Also cap concurrent prefetches per-host to avoid bursting PCIe.

Rachel Meyers: +1. Also add a NUMA-fallback: if preferred node is saturated, we can route new allocations to remote NUMA but mark them as remote_resident and schedule background migration when host idle. That avoids immediate failures.

Ava Morgan: Good. Implementation sketch:
```
alloc(key, size, preferred_numa=auto, tier=VRAM) -> handle
on_access(handle) -> increment sample counter
background: if counter > prefetch_th && handle.tier==VRAM && !resident_on_preferred -> prefetch_to(preferred)
evictor: order by (sticky? + last_access_age + numa_penalty)
```
We need numa_penalty tuning so that hot pages on non-preferred nodes aren't evicted too aggressively.

Liam O'Connor: Also consider fragmentation: NUMA-aware allocation increases small-run fragmentation on some nodes. We should track per-node frag_score and run incremental coalesce per-node (cheap) rather than global compaction. Coalesce can be limited to nodes with frag_score>0.6.

Hiro Tanaka: Microbench on prototype (mixed long-context + embeddings):
```
baseline: p95=48ms, tail-work p99=210ms, remote_access_rate=3.2%
numa-prefetch (no cap): p95=44ms, p99=260ms, pci-bus spike seen
numa-prefetch (cap prefetches=8): p95=46ms, p99=220ms, remote_access_rate=1.1%
```
Conclusion: cap and backpressure are critical.

Rachel Meyers: Operator side: expose metrics per-node: node_frag_score, node_resident_percent, prefetch_inflight, remote_migrations/sec. Alert if prefetch_inflight>cap*1.2 or node_frag_score>0.7.

Ava Morgan: Rollout plan: feature-flag memory.numa_prefetch disabled by default. Canary on 2 hosts with cap=4, demote_after_ms=120000, per-node coalesce enabled. Gates: p95, p99, pcie-util, node_frag_score. Owners: Hiro proto, Liam sims, Rachel telemetry + alerts.

infra-bot: feature-flag memory.numa_prefetch created. Canary scheduled: group=numa-canary start=Mon 05:00 UTC. Dashboards: /d/memory/numa-prefetch (owner: @Rachel).

Liam O'Connor: I'll run mixed-workload sims with Q4_replay + heavy_tail. Will test worst-case: many small allocations pinned to same NUMA to see frag amplification.

Hiro Tanaka: I'll add prefetch backoff logic: exponential backoff per-handle if prefetch fails due to PCIe pressure. Also emit prefetch_failure metric so we can tune caps.

Rachel Meyers: I'll add a tenant-level NUMA heatmap so we can see when a tenant is concentrating hot keys on a node. Might surface bad client patterns.

Ava Morgan: Action items tracked. Keep sticky/perm pins off until we validate demotion and coalesce. Ping this thread with sim links and dashboard screenshots. :+1:

Hiro Tanaka: Will post sim links by EOD.

infra-bot: canary created (id: canary-2026-09-07-02).
